text:
liz_sales: Heads-up — Acme procurement back. They want PO net-90 (ouch), sign via their vendor portal (DocuX), and they've redlined the DPA to remove our subprocessor clause. Also requested KMS hosted in EU and custom SLA 99.95% with financial credits. Can legal/finance advise on approach? @kevin_legal @marco_finance

ashok_se: For the POC we're on hosted API; we can pin region eu-west1 and enable customer-managed keys in our private offering, but that takes ~2 weeks to provision. For short-term POC we'd propose data not persisted + ephemeral keys. Is that acceptable to procurement?

kevin_legal: Please drop their redline here. High-level: removing subprocessor transparency is a showstopper. We can offer a limited subprocessor disclosure instead. SLA credit language — avoid unlimited liability and keep aggregate cap. Net-90: if customer insists, require PO plus a one-time up-front deposit equal to 30% of first-month commit and credit check. Will loop in sales leadership if they push Net-90.

liz_sales: attaching redline -> https://acme.internal/procurement/redlines/ACME-DPA-v2.pdf

dana_legal: Quick strategy: 1) push back on removing subprocessor clause; offer a tailored paragraph listing major subprocessors + 30-days notice; 2) keep SLA credits tied to monthly invoice, cap at 3x monthly fees; 3) for KMS, offer EU KMS for Dedicated/Private only — provide SOC2 + encryption in transit at rest for hosted POC; 4) net-90 -> require finance mitigations or escalate.

marco_finance: Net-90 is hard for us at scale. Options: a) 30% deposit up-front b) shorter Net-30 with auto-invoice on PO creation c) invoice factoring with partner (we can propose). Which does sales want to offer?

liz_sales: Customer prefers no upfront payment. Can we offer conditional Net-90: first POC month 30% deposit, subsequent months Net-60 after credit check? Also need signer fallback — their portal fails for cross-org signers. Any standard fallback for DocuSign/DocuSign Connect?

kevin_legal: Signer fallback: require counterparty to accept DocuSign or Adobe Sign. If their portal blocks, we can send DocuSign envelope to their authorized signer. Add a flow in order form: "If customer vendor portal prevents execution, parties will accept execution via DocuSign." Keep it short.

ashok_se: For technical note to procurement: here's the POC orderline snippet they asked for:
```
Order line: Redwood Inference Hosted POC — 10k tokens/day, eu-west1 region, non-persistent logs, evaluation-only data retention = 7 days. Pricing: $X/mo trial credit. Acceptance: success criteria agreed in SOW.
```

liz_sales: Thanks all. Next steps: kevin/dana draft redline response (target EOD), marco propose payment path, ashok confirm region/keys timeline. I'll update customer and try to avoid immediate escalation. :pray:

deploy-bot: SOC2 report link: https://redwood.internal/compliance/SOC2-2025.pdf (access restricted)
